The residue of $-37$ modulo $5$ is the integer $0\le r<5$ such that

$$
-37≡r\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $-37$ as an integer multiple of $5,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $-37≡3\,(\text{mod}\,5)$ because

$$
-37=(-8)\cdot 5+3.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-37$ modulo $5$ is $3.$

**Method 2**

We can use the addition property:

$$
\begin{aligned}-37 & ≡-37+0 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡-37+8\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡-37+40 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-37$ modulo $5$ is $3.$
